sentences.text: The premise is true: the Board accepted Huang's resignation as President, CEO and director on November 11, 2026, effective immediately, and named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO.

The step from that departure to a reason to buy has nothing behind it in the record; no finding or analytic connects a CEO change to later earnings, cash flow or valuation, and the claim rests on a cause the facts cannot test.
The three corollaries all hold, but each compares the quarter ended 2026-07-26 with earlier quarters, so they describe the business before the resignation and cannot be credited to Huang's absence.
The valuation analytics use a price dated 2026-09-30, also before the departure, so the record does not show how the market priced the change or what the price is now.

What that pre-departure price already required is demanding: 13.4% a year for 10 years, a pace 0 of 40 comparable large-filer spans matched, and it leans most on the 65.2% operating margin holding every year, since at the industry's 90th percentile margin of 26.6% the need rises to 28.1%.

The exit also sits among other 2026 senior departures, the head of worldwide field operations and the chief accounting officer, so the record shows leadership turnover, not a change it can identify as an improvement.

The interim leadership inherits a business whose operating margin, revenue growth and cost discipline were all improving in the latest reported quarter, so the departure does not arrive on a weakening record.
The interim CEO is the sitting CFO rather than an outsider, which at least keeps the financial reporting chain inside existing management.
The 8-K gives no reason for the resignation and names only an interim successor, so the thesis treats as positive an event whose cause and outcome the record leaves open.
Because the price already needed the trailing margin to hold for a decade, any loss of execution after a founder-CEO exit would hit the assumption the valuation leans on most.
Revenue growth of +105.9% in the latest quarter was achieved before the departure, so citing strong results as support for the claim credits the change with performance it did not produce.
The claim turns on a cause the record cannot test: whether the company does better without Huang, which only filings for quarters after November 11, 2026 could begin to show.
It also turns on who leads permanently, which no 8-K in the record yet states.
And it turns on whether the margin the price leans on survives the transition.

conditions.text: An 8-K naming a permanent CEO would replace the interim arrangement and give the first evidence of the post-Huang leadership.
A post-resignation quarter with operating margin below the 65.2% trailing level the reverse DCF assumes would cut against the claim that the departure is a reason to buy.
A post-resignation quarter with gross margin below 70% would break the run tested in claim c2 under new leadership.
